source.version: arXiv:2502.09577v2, 12 August 2025; journal-formatted manuscript bearing November 2025 publication information
source.title_on_document: Polymind: Parallel Visual Diagramming with Large Language Models to Support Prewriting Through Microtasks

paper_design_summary: A formative study observed 10 writing-related students planning stories with GPT-3 and pen and paper; the system description also mentions an earlier pilot without its sample or allocation details (PDF p. 6, Sections 3-3.1; p. 14, Section 6.2.1; p. 16, Section 6.4). In the main evaluation, 10 university-recruited writers used both Polymind and GPT-4 & Canvas for story ideation and outlining, with a Latin square balancing prompts and systems but no statement of random assignment to sequences (PDF pp. 17-18, Sections 7.1-7.2.3). The researchers reported idea counts and had two expert writers score the outlines using TTCW (PDF pp. 18 and 20, Sections 7.2.3 and 7.3.2).

assignment.what_was_assigned: All participants were asked to complete the same LLM-assisted story-planning activity with pen and paper. No comparison condition or assignment of different AI assistance is described.
assignment.quote: After participants consented to the study, we asked them to develop a science fiction or thriller story plot using an LLM together with the traditional tools (a pen and a piece of paper) for diagramming or illustrating their ideas.

arms.name: GPT-3 playground with pen and paper
arms.description: Single activity: participants used the GPT-3 playground and pen-and-paper diagrams to develop a story plot (PDF p. 6, Section 3.1).

participants.who: Students in writing- or creativity-related majors recruited through snowball sampling, with daily writing habits; ethnically Chinese and English second-language speakers. Think-aloud and reflection transcripts were analyzed thematically.
participants.quote: To understand how large language models could support diagramming-based prewriting, we conducted a formative study involving 10 participants with daily writing habits ranging from news articles to fiction writing.
participants.locator: PDF p. 6 (316:6), Sections 3 Formative Study and 3.1 Protocol.

ai_tool.how_used: Participants used the LLM alongside pen-and-paper diagramming, thinking aloud while developing story plots (PDF p. 6, Section 3.1).

task.description: Develop a science-fiction or thriller story plot and illustrate ideas with pen and paper. The reported analysis concerns collaboration experiences and strategies; no creativity score on the output is reported (PDF pp. 6-7, Sections 3.1-3.3).

studies.label: Earlier system pilot: briefly mentioned, sample not reported

assignment.what_was_assigned: Allocation, comparison conditions and condition order are not reported for the earlier pilot mentioned during the system description.
assignment.locator: PDF p. 14 (316:14), Section 6.2.1 Inferring User Attention; p. 16 (316:16), Section 6.4 Implementation.

arms.name: Early Polymind system
arms.description: The paper mentions users of an earlier system pilot but does not specify experimental arms (PDF p. 14, Section 6.2.1).

participants.who: Users of an earlier system pilot; sample size, recruitment, demographics and overlap with the other studies are not reported.
participants.quote: In an earlier pilot study of our system, we found that users might lose track of generation results if a microtask was constantly operating on diagram nodes far away from users’ focus of attention.

ai_tool.name_model: Earlier Polymind system; pilot-specific model not stated
ai_tool.how_used: The pilot informed attention-sensitive operation of microtasks and their timing; the paper does not separately specify the pilot AI setup (PDF p. 14, Section 6.2.1; p. 16, Section 6.4).

task.description: Specific pilot task instructions are not reported. The reported observation concerns users losing track of microtask results when operations were distant from their focus of attention (PDF p. 14, Section 6.2.1).

studies.label: Main evaluation: Polymind versus GPT-4 & Canvas

assignment.what_was_assigned: The sequence of writing prompts and system conditions was balanced with a Latin square. Every participant used both systems; random assignment of people to sequences or randomization of condition order is not stated. This is a within-person controlled comparison with unresolved randomization.
assignment.quote: We used a Latin square experimental design [72] to achieve a balanced sequence of writing prompts and system conditions.
assignment.locator: PDF p. 18 (316:18), Section 7.2.2 Conditions and Section 7.2.3 Study Procedure.

arms.name: Polymind
arms.description: Full Polymind with six predefined microtasks, using GPT-4; the same participants also completed the baseline condition (PDF p. 16, Section 6.4; p. 18, Sections 7.2.2-7.2.3; pp. 20-21, Section 7.3.3 and Table 2).

arms.name: GPT-4 & Canvas
arms.description: ChatGPT-4 conversational interface plus the Polymind diagramming canvas, with microtasking features turned off; the same participants also completed Polymind (PDF pp. 17-18, Sections 7.1-7.2.3).

participants.who: Convenience sample mainly from local universities, with creative-writing experience or related majors; L2 English speakers, experienced with prewriting or diagramming tools, and with limited AI or programming knowledge. The paper does not explicitly identify every participant as a student. These are the same people in both conditions, not separate samples.
participants.quote: We used convenience sampling to recruit 10 participants (4 male, 6 female) mainly from local universities.
participants.locator: PDF p. 17 (316:17), Section 7.1 Participants; p. 18 (316:18), Section 7.2.3 (both systems per participant); p. 20 (316:20), Section 7.3.3 (10 participants produced final results); p. 21 (316:21), Table 2 (V1-V10).

ai_tool.how_used: Polymind provided configurable parallel microtasks for brainstorming, elaboration, summarizing, drafting, freewriting and association on a diagramming canvas, with proactive/reactive modes. The baseline allowed conversational ChatGPT-4 use plus a canvas without AI microtasks (PDF p. 16, Section 6.4; pp. 17-18, Section 7.2.2).

task.description: For each system, brainstorm distinct storylines from a creative-writing prompt, then choose a favorite storyline and prepare a detailed outline with structure and key events. Prompts concerned traveling an endless road and running away from something (PDF pp. 17-18, Sections 7.2.1-7.2.3).
task.duration: 12 minutes per story-ideation or story-outlining session; four sessions per participant across both systems (PDF p. 18, Section 7.2.3).

outcomes.name: Torrance Test of Creative Writing (TTCW): tests passed by story outlines
outcomes.question: with_ai

contrasts.reported: Two expert writers scored the outlines. The text reports 5.7 TTCW tests passed for GPT-4 & Canvas (baseline), compared with 4 for Polymind (P = 0.23). The text does not specify the statistical test or aggregation across raters.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 18 (316:18), Section 7.2.3 (expert scoring); p. 20 (316:20), Section 7.3.2 Creativity Support and Figure 12 (reported comparison).

outcomes.name: Number of ideas produced during story ideation
outcomes.question: with_ai

contrasts.reported: Polymind median = 3, stdev = 1.06; baseline (GPT-4 & Canvas) median = 3, stdev = 8.51. The text describes similar numbers of ideas and gives no p-value for this comparison. The baseline stdev of 8.51 is reproduced as printed in the PDF.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 20 (316:20), Section 7.3.2 Creativity Support, opening paragraph.

eligibility.reason: The main evaluation analyzes 10 people, each using both AI configurations, so it fails the 50-person threshold (PDF p. 17, Section 7.1; p. 18, Section 7.2.3; pp. 20-21, Section 7.3.3 and Table 2). Latin-square counterbalancing is stated, but random assignment to sequences or randomized order is not stated; criterion 1 is therefore unclear and the design is coded other (PDF p. 18, Section 7.2.2). Output scoring is present through expert TTCW scores and idea counts (PDF pp. 18 and 20, Sections 7.2.3 and 7.3.2). The formative study has 10 participants and qualitative analysis; the briefly mentioned pilot has no reported sample size or scored creativity outcome (PDF p. 6, Sections 3-3.1; p. 14, Section 6.2.1; p. 16, Section 6.4). No qualifying observational, AI-versus-human, or synthesis context dataset is identified.

one_line_finding: In the 10-person evaluation, Polymind outlines passed 4 TTCW tests versus 5.7 for GPT-4 & Canvas (P = 0.23), while both conditions produced a median of 3 ideas (PDF p. 17, Section 7.1; p. 20, Section 7.3.2).
